item.title: Superior Court honors and bids farewell to Patrick Diaz
item.description: (Press Release) — The CNMI Superior Court honors the contributions of Clerk of the Superior Court Patrick V. Diaz as he moves into the next stage of his professional life. The post Superior Court honors and bids farewell to Patrick Diaz appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: DEQ replaces older diesel operated equipment
item.description: (DEQ) — The Bureau of Environmental and Coastal Quality’s Division of Environmental Quality announced recent progress in reducing harmful diesel emissions through the Diesel Emissions Reduction Act or DERA State Grants, a federal funding program administered by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. The post DEQ replaces older diesel operated equipment appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Rota SBDC completes federal contracting training for local businesses
item.description: (SBDC) — The Rota Small Business Development Center recently completed a no-cost federal contracting training on Jan. 13 and 14, 2026, at the Northern Marianas College Rota Center Computer Lab. The post Rota SBDC completes federal contracting training for local businesses appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: CNMI SBDC Network opens call for exhibitors for 2026 CNMI Industry Day
item.description: (SBDC) — The CNMI Small Business Development Center Network at Northern Marianas College is now accepting exhibitor registrations for CNMI Industry Day 2026, a three-day, tri-island event designed to connect local businesses with federal agencies, military partners, and major contractors operating in the region. The post CNMI SBDC Network opens call for exhibitors for 2026 CNMI Industry Day appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Tinian homestead permits under review
item.description: THE Tinian District Office of the Department of Public Lands is informing participants of the agriculture homestead lottery held on Aug. 19 and 20, 2025, that all homestead permits are currently undergoing legal review to ensure legal sufficiency and compliance with applicable rules and regulations. The post Tinian homestead permits under review appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Mayors seek civilian plans amid Tinian military expansion
item.description: AS reconstruction of World War II-era airstrips at Tinian’s North Field accelerates amid intensifying military rivalry with China, the mayors of Tinian, Saipan and Rota say they are watching developments closely and are anxious about what lies ahead for their constituents should a conflict occur. The post Mayors seek civilian plans amid Tinian military expansion appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: OAG adopts regulations ‘to strengthen investigative subpoena process’
item.description: (Press Release) — The Office of the Attorney General on Thursday adopted regulations establishing a clear and fair process for the use of investigative subpoenas, a critical tool that ensures thorough, just, and efficient criminal investigations. The post OAG adopts regulations ‘to strengthen investigative subpoena process’ appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Ralph, Vinnie to face off in GOP gubernatorial primary
item.description: The Republican Party of the Northern Mariana Islands announced that its Executive Committee convened and certified that two letters of intent have been duly submitted by former Sen. Vinnie Flores Sablan and former Gov. Ralph Deleon Guerrero Torres, each seeking the party’s endorsement to run for governor of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. The post Ralph, Vinnie to face off in GOP gubernatorial primary appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Maisie Tenorio is BOE’s new chair
item.description: MAISIE B. Tenorio was elected chair of the CNMI Board of Education on Thursday, succeeding Aschumar Kodep Ogumoro-Uludong. The post Maisie Tenorio is BOE’s new chair appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: CNMI mayors call for federal action to revive economy
item.description: THE mayors of Saipan, Tinian, and Rota have issued two joint letters calling for urgent federal intervention to revive the Commonwealth’s faltering economy and opposing proposed seabed mining in CNMI waters, citing threats to the environment and cultural heritage. The post CNMI mayors call for federal action to revive economy appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.
